text: Vernalization, the requirement for prolonged winter cold before flowering that is remembered through stable chromatin silencing of the FLC gene, is presented as the clearest and best-characterized example of plant memory.
explanation: True. In Arabidopsis, cold drives progressive PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 silencing of FLC that is stably maintained through subsequent cell divisions, permitting flowering in spring. The book treats it as the clearest example of adaptive, long-term epigenetic memory implemented entirely without a nervous system.
